slides.heading: Class Photos
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Easy · Greedy Algorithms
slides.narration: Let's solve Class Photos, an easy greedy algorithms problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Equal numbers of red and blue shirted students; all of one colour in the back row, each back-row student strictly taller than the person in front.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Equal numbers of red and blue shirted students; all of one colour in the back row, each back-row student strictly taller than the person in front. Is a photo possible?

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: The taller group must stand in the back, and then every back student must be taller than the one in front.
slides.narration: Sort both groups. The taller group must stand in the back, and then every back student must be taller than the one in front.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. The group with the taller tallest goes in the back
slides.narration: Step by step. First, sort red and blue shirts. Second, the group with the taller tallest goes in the back. Third, check every pair strictly. Fourth, any failure means false.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n log n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Recap
slides.narration: To recap Class Photos: Sort both groups. The taller group must stand in the back, and then every back student must be taller than the one in front. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
